structure.overview: The case concerns the reasonableness of delay between conviction and sentencing under section 11(b) of the Charter, with the appellant challenging the sentencing delay as unreasonable. The appellant argues for a five-month presumptive ceiling on sentencing delay, following the Ontario Court of Appeal's Charley decision, while the Crown and the Supreme Court prefer a flexible, contextual 'markedly longer than reasonable' test. The Supreme Court rejects presumptive ceilings for sentencing delay, adopts the flexible markedly longer test, and upholds the lower court's approach to assessing delay reasonableness.

summaries.speaker: below
summaries.summary: Defence requested adjournment for trial transcript; sentencing submissions scheduled for February 25, 2022, by trial judge.

summaries.speaker: below
summaries.summary: On February 25, 2022, defence made submissions; Crown could not submit due to technical delays; hearing continued to April 5, 2022.

summaries.speaker: below
summaries.summary: On April 5, 2022, another judge adjourned due to trial judge unavailability; rescheduled to April 19, 2022 for Crown submissions.

summaries.speaker: below
summaries.summary: On May 24, 2022, trial judge questioned counsel; Crown to provide written responses; next hearing set for July 12, 2022.

summaries.speaker: below
summaries.summary: On July 12, 2022, another judge adjourned due to trial judge emergency; rescheduled to September 16, 2022.

summaries.speaker: below
summaries.summary: On September 16, 2022, trial judge not ready to sentence, sought immigration clarification; continuation set for October 20, 2022.

summaries.speaker: below
summaries.summary: On October 20, 2022, defence filed stay application for unreasonable sentencing delay under s. 11(b); appellant waived delay for Crown response.

summaries.speaker: below
summaries.summary: On December 16, 2022, trial judge dismissed s. 11(b) application and sentenced appellant to conditional sentence and probation.

summaries.speaker: below
summaries.summary: Trial judge found 378-day sentencing delay, deducted 74 days for defence adjournment, 80 days for unavailability, 69 days for complexity, 39 days for submissions delay.

summaries.speaker: below
summaries.summary: Trial judge concluded net sentencing delay was 116 days, under Charley's five-month ceiling, and dismissed s. 11(b) application.

citations.why: Presumptive ceiling for post-verdict delay

summaries.speaker: below
summaries.summary: Court of Appeal found net sentencing delay was 225 days, exceeding Charley's ceiling, and held s. 11(b) rights were infringed.

citations.why: Five-month presumptive ceiling for post-verdict delay

summaries.speaker: below
summaries.summary: Court of Appeal reduced sentence due to delay, rejected conditional discharge, and noted immigration consequences were considered.
